rules: Quote only from page snapshots (snap/), never from full.md, the faq index or the changes feed text.

Two namespaces: CloudFront facts use service key cloudfront and ids starting cloudfront- (sub-prefixes help: cloudfront-quota-, cloudfront-oac-, cloudfront-signed-, cloudfront-fn-, cloudfront-lambda-edge-, cloudfront-tls-, cloudfront-change-, cloudfront-faq-, cloudfront-price-). Global Accelerator facts use service key global-accelerator and ids starting global-accelerator- (two facts already exist: global-accelerator-standard-endpoint-types, global-accelerator-decision-guide-gaming-iot-voip; do not duplicate them).

Put facts in files of 10 to 25, named facts-<lens>-NN.json in _build/work/15-cloudfront/, and add them with: python3 aws-saa-book/tools/saa.py facts add --file <file> --by <your label>. Keep every quote verbatim (copy it from saa.py show output).

Each demand item lists look_in source ids; record it as filled (with fact ids), contradicted (with what the page says) or not-found, in mine-<lens>.json (shape: {"lens", "by", "items": [{"id", "status", "facts": [], "note"}]}).

Quota numbers come from the quota tables: use facts adopt --source <id> --table N --row M (indexes as printed by saa.py tables) so that the value is known to sit under 'Default quota'. CloudFront quota tables: 0 general, 1 distributions, 2 policies, 4 CloudFront Functions, 6 key value stores, 7 and 8 Lambda@Edge, 9 SSL certificates, 10 invalidations, 11 key groups, 12 WebSocket, 13 field-level encryption, 16 headers. Global Accelerator: table 0 general, table 1 endpoints per endpoint group.
A display of a number-free fact is a short phrase (at most 8 words) copied verbatim from a quote (RULINGS 2026-10-11).
Behavior, capability, restriction and default facts need at least two displays (gate B12).

A change fact carries its date from the document-history row (quote the row; table_header from the history table); the old value only when the history row, the What's New item or a page states it verbatim. Anything GA after 2026-07-15 is labelled not examinable yet (note field).

Prices are volatile: set volatility to volatile on every dollar amount and on edge-location counts. The CloudFront pricing page (www/cloudfront/pricing) now shows the flat-rate plans; pay-as-you-go text is on www/cloudfront/pricing/pay-as-you-go (check whether its price tables are in the static text before quoting a dollar amount; if not, mine dimensions and billing rules only).

Facts already owned by other chapters (link, do not duplicate): ACM on CloudFront (acm-cloudfront-us-east-1, acm-faq-cloudfront-us-east-1, acm-cloudfront-one-cert-per-distribution, acm-cloudfront-same-cert-many-distributions, acm-cloudfront-origin-certificate-any-region, acm-cloudfront-managed-certificates, acm-http-validation-cloudfront-only, acm-change-http-validation-cloudfront-2025), WAF on CloudFront (waf-cloudfront-*), Shield (shield-standard-every-region-edge, shield-standard-best-on-edge-resources, shield-protect-sites-outside-aws-via-cloudfront), Lambda@Edge from the Lambda side (lambda-faq-edge-*, lambda-edge-*), S3 side (s3-cloudfront-oai-bucket-policy, s3-website-sse-kms-needs-cloudfront-oac, s3-faq-ta-vs-cloudfront, s3-transfer-acceleration-*, s3-pricing-data-transfer-to-cloudfront-free, s3-war-avoid-public-buckets-use-cloudfront, s3-faq-mrap-global-accelerator), ELB side (elb-alb-cloudfront-prefix-list-sg, elb-cloudfront-vpc-origins-*, elb-change-cloudfront-vpc-origins-2024-11, elb-alb-global-accelerator-static-ips), global infrastructure (global-infrastructure-*). Each demand item names the relevant ones in link_existing.
Do not quote the unusable pages listed in brief.v0.json (generic case-study listings, the retired secure-content-delivery whitepaper redirect, the DDoS whitepaper abstract).

numbers.what: Every quota, default, range, timeout, size, count and pricing dimension of CloudFront and Global Accelerator: distribution quotas, cache behaviors and origins, file size, RPS and bandwidth, CNAMEs, origin timeouts, TTL defaults, invalidation quotas and free paths, error caching TTL, key groups, CloudFront Functions and Lambda@Edge limits, KeyValueStore, policy quotas, certificate quotas and key sizes, field-level encryption, Anycast static IP count, logs, price classes, pricing dimensions, free tier, flat-rate plans, SLAs, compression range, GA quotas, static IP counts, traffic dial and weight ranges, health check settings, failover speed, GA pricing, idle timeouts, custom routing, BYOIP, edge location counts, signed URL policy options, WebSocket quota.

behavior.what: How CloudFront and Global Accelerator work: request flow and regional edge caches, origin types, cache behaviors, viewer and origin protocol policies, certificates and SNI, security policies, end-to-end HTTPS, field-level encryption, mTLS, OAC and OAI, website endpoints, VPC origins, ALB restriction, signed URLs and cookies, key groups, geo restriction, cache key and policies, TTL headers, cache hit ratio, invalidation vs versioning, origin failover, custom errors, Origin Shield, HTTP methods, dynamic acceleration, WebSockets and gRPC, WAF and Shield attachment, CloudFront Functions vs Lambda@Edge, triggers and restrictions, KeyValueStore, edge locations and global service guidance, Anycast static IPs, continuous deployment, multi-tenant distributions, streaming, zone apex; GA definition, components, health checks and failover, traffic dials and weights, client IP preservation, client affinity, custom routing, resilience, DNS and IPv6, internal endpoints, EIP comparison, ELB integration, cross-account and BYOIP, monitoring, performance mechanism, Regions and control plane.

decisions+changes.what: Comparisons the exam hinges on (CloudFront vs Global Accelerator, GA vs DNS failover, Transfer Acceleration vs CloudFront, Lambda@Edge vs CloudFront Functions, OAC vs signed URL/cookie vs geo restriction vs WAF), cost routes (4.4.S3), CDN strategy (4.4.S4), DDoS whitepaper edge guidance, every dated change since mid-2022 with the 'not examinable yet' cut at 2026-07-15, Callvale's month-11 decision and stage-4 live-audio decision, and real-world case quotes.
decisions+changes.feed: python3 aws-saa-book/tools/saa.py changes for cloudfront --verbose  (and global-accelerator); history rows are quotable from docs/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/WhatsNew and docs/global-accelerator/latest/dg/WhatsNew; What's New items give dates only, never quotes. Lists: changes-cloudfront.txt, changes-ga.txt.

faq.what: FAQ items worth a quick-fire question, quoted verbatim from the FAQ page snapshots (the FAQ quick-fire section of 2-deep.md needs 10 items; mine at least 20 so the writer can choose). Use saa.py faq <url> --find TEXT to locate an item, then quote from snap with saa.py show www/cloudfront/faqs --around TEXT.
faq.feed: _build/corpus/faq/cloudfront.jsonl and _build/corpus/faq/global-accelerator.jsonl (question positions in faq-list-cloudfront.txt and faq-list-ga.txt)

notes: All 155 planned sources are in the corpus; nothing failed. Six URLs are unusable (see brief.v0.json unusable_pages).

A hit in full:amazoncloudfront-developerguide or full:global-accelerator-dg is a pointer, not evidence; fetch the page with saa.py fetch and quote from snap/. Pages not fetched yet (for example cache-hit details, Lambda@Edge tutorials, connection functions, invalidation-by-tags) may be fetched on demand; add them to a urls-7.txt list.

Demand items that span lenses (for example d024 flat-rate plans and d130 its change note, d062 OAC and d127 the OAC change note) are split on purpose: the numbers or behavior lens mines the current truth, the decisions+changes lens mines only the dated change.

Change items dated after 2026-07-15 (OAC for S3 Multi-Region Access Points 2026-08-20, flat-rate plan API 2026-09-03, Dynamic Image Transformation 2026-09-08) are labelled not examinable yet. CloudFront Functions logging to access logs is 2026-07-14, one day before the cut: record the date and let the writer decide.
Hypotheses in the brief come from memory and FREQUENCY/FRESHNESS; they are questions, never evidence. If a page contradicts one, record the page's value and mark the item contradicted.

Callvale facts (70% static requests, 20% users outside the US, 5-minute playback links) are story numbers from STARTUP.md and are never mined; only the AWS behaviour behind the decision is mined (d136, d137).
